elements.element: Transition assistance obligation triggered on expiry or termination
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) ... provide reasonable transition assistance"

elements.element: Assistance available for up to 6 months
elements.evidence: "for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date"

elements.element: Return of Customer Data within 30 days
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) days after the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content, user information, customer data and other Company data"

elements.element: Return in a standard machine-readable format
Deletion of Customer Data after return
elements.evidence: "(c) thereafter delete such Content, information and data from its systems"
"and certify such deletion to the Company in writing"

elements.element: At least 90 days of transition assistance
elements.evidence: "up to six (6) months following the Termination Date" (exceeds 90 days)
"within thirty (30) days after the Termination Date, return to the Company all ... Company data"

reasons: The inserted Section 4.3 supplies every preferred atomic element: assistance on expiry or termination, up to six months, at then-current rates, 30-day return of Company data in a machine-readable format, then deletion plus written certification.

The request condition ("at the Company's request") attaches only to limb (a) assistance; limbs (b) return and (c) deletion/certification remain unconditional, so the mandatory data-return mechanic is not swallowed.
"commonly used, machine-readable format" is a literal equivalent of the preferred "standard machine-readable format"; no material shortfall.

Minor drafting note only: the 30-day and 6-month clocks run from the defined "Termination Date," which 4.1 defines by reference to a termination notice, so on simple expiry the reference point is imprecise; consider "expiration or termination" as the trigger date. This is a wording refinement, not a failure of the position.
"Content" is used as a capitalised term; confirm it is defined elsewhere in the Agreement to avoid an undefined reference.
Insertion is a single new section addressing an absent clause; nothing existing was altered, so minimality and intent are preserved.
